cues.zh: 今天的嘉宾视频来自Practical Engineering频道的Grady。
cues.en: Today’s guest video is from Grady at Practical Engineering.

cues.zh: 他讲述了一场悲剧：
cues.en: He’s talking about a tragedy:

cues.zh: 我们从中吸取的教训以及事故发生的原因都非常引人深思。
cues.en: and the lessons we learned and the reasons why it happened are fascinating.

cues.zh: 他还自己制作了道具。
cues.en: Also, he made his own props.

cues.zh: Grady，交给你了。
cues.en: Grady, take it away.

cues.zh: 1981年夏天，密苏里州堪萨斯城的凯悦酒店
cues.en: In the summer of 1981, the Hyatt Regency Hotel in Kansas City, Missouri,

cues.zh: 在多层中庭区域举办了一场大型聚会。
cues.en: hosted a large party in the multi-story atrium area.

cues.zh: 活动期间，
cues.en: During the event,

cues.zh: 二楼和四楼的悬挂式走廊坍塌，
cues.en: suspended walkways on the second and fourth floors collapsed,

cues.zh: 造成100多人死亡，200多人受伤。
cues.en: killing over 100 people and injuring over 200 more.

cues.zh: 当时，这是美国历史上最严重的结构失效事故。
cues.en: At the time, the accident was the worst structural failure in US history.

cues.zh: 灾难发生后，
cues.en: In the wake of the disaster,

cues.zh: 调查人员发现走廊的原始设计被更改过，
cues.en: investigators discovered a change to the original design of the walkways

cues.zh: 这一更改由制造商提出，并被结构工程师错误批准。
cues.en: that was proposed by the fabricator and mistakenly approved by the structural engineer.

cues.zh: 乍看之下，这似乎只是对设计做了一处细微的调整，
cues.en: What, at first glance, seemed like a subtle adjustment to the design,

cues.zh: 结果却是导致事故的根本原因。
cues.en: turned out to be the root cause of the failure.

cues.zh: 凯悦酒店的中庭里横跨着两条悬空步道，
cues.en: Two suspended walkways spanned the atrium in the Hyatt Regency

cues.zh: 二层步道正好位于四层步道正下方。
cues.en: with the second-floor walkway directly below the fourth-floor walkway.

cues.zh: 每条步道都由一系列箱形梁支撑，
cues.en: Each was supported by a series of box girders

cues.zh: 这些箱形梁由吊杆悬挂，并用螺母和垫圈固定。
cues.en: suspended by hanger rods and retained by nuts and washers.

cues.zh: 最初的设计要求使用一对吊杆，
cues.en: The original design called for a single pair of hanger rods,

cues.zh: 穿过每一根四层箱形梁，连接到下方的二层箱形梁。
cues.en: which would pass through each fourth-floor girder to the second-floor girder below.

cues.zh: 负责建造步道的制造商反对这个方案，
cues.en: The fabricator responsible for constructing the walkways objected to this plan

cues.zh: 因为这样吊杆全长都需要加工螺纹，
cues.en: because it would require screw threads for the entire length of the hanger rods,

cues.zh: 而这些螺纹在施工过程中很容易受损。
cues.en: which could easily be damaged during construction.

cues.zh: 于是，他们提议把吊杆分成两组。
cues.en: So, they proposed to split the hanger rods into two sets.

cues.zh: 一组把四层通道连到屋顶，
cues.en: One to connect the fourth-floor walkway to the roof

cues.zh: 另一组把二层通道连到四层的横梁上。
cues.en: and one to connect the second-floor walkway up to the fourth-floor girders.

cues.zh: 如果你没看出这个改动有多关键，那你并不孤单。
cues.en: If you don’t notice the significance of this change, you’re not alone.

cues.zh: 工程师没做详细审查或计算就批准了，
cues.en: It was approved by the engineer without a detailed review or calculations,

cues.zh: 而这些本可以揭示其固有缺陷。
cues.en: which would have revealed its inherent flaw.

cues.zh: 在这个布置中，也就是原设计，
cues.en: In this setup, which represents the original design,

cues.zh: 两条通道的荷载是各自独立传递给吊杆的。
cues.en: the load of the two walkways is independently transferred to the hanger rods.

cues.zh: 注意，我可以抬起任一根横梁而不影响另一根。
cues.en: Notice how I can lift each girder without affecting the other.

cues.zh: 现在，看看这个设计改动。
cues.en: Now, let’s look at the design change.

cues.zh: 在这个构造中，
cues.en: In this configuration,

cues.zh: 注意二层通道的全部重量承受者
cues.en: notice that the entire weight of the second-floor walkway is being borne

cues.zh: 并不是吊杆，
cues.en: not directly by the hanger rod,

cues.zh: 而是上方的横梁。
cues.en: but instead, by the girder above.

cues.zh: 如果我把四楼的走道抬起来，二楼的走道也会跟着被抬起。
cues.en: If I lift the fourth-floor walkway, the second-floor walkway is lifted as well.

cues.zh: 吊杆顶部承受的荷载仍然相同，
cues.en: The hanger rods are still carrying the same load at the top,

cues.zh: 但上层大梁上的两个螺母却在支撑两条走道的重量。
cues.en: but the two nuts on the upper girder are supporting the weight of both walkways.

cues.zh: 这个看似简单的改动，实际上使那些螺栓连接处的荷载翻了一倍。
cues.en: This simple change effectively doubled the load on those bolted connections.

cues.zh: 想象一下，你和一位朋友都抓在一根绳子上。
cues.en: Imagine that you and a friend are both hanging on a rope.

cues.zh: 原设计相当于你们俩各自独立地抓住绳子，
cues.en: The original design is the equivalent of you both holding onto the rope independently,

cues.zh: 而改动后的设计则相当于你的朋友抓着你的脚踝。
cues.en: whereas the design change is the equivalent of your friend hanging onto your ankles.

cues.zh: 两种情况下绳子承受的总重量是一样的，
cues.en: The total weight supported by the rope is the same in both cases,

cues.zh: 但你保持抓握的可能性却不同了。
cues.en: but your likelihood of maintaining a grip is not.

cues.zh: 调查人员认定，这一不易察觉的改动是导致失效的主要原因。
cues.en: This subtle change was identified by investigators as the primary cause of failure.

cues.zh: 那天晚上，步道上挤满了人，
cues.en: With so many people on the walkways that evening,

cues.zh: 连接处承受的荷载过大。
cues.en: the load on the connections was too great.

cues.zh: 箱形梁裂开，滑过垫圈和螺母，
cues.en: The box girders split open, slipping past the washers and nuts

cues.zh: 导致两条步道都坍塌了。
cues.en: leading to the collapse of both walkways.

cues.zh: 社会与工程师之间有一种不言而喻的信任。
cues.en: There is an implicit handshake between a society and its engineers.

cues.zh: 我们几乎只能相信，我们生活其中的人造环境
cues.en: We hardly have a choice but to trust that the constructed environment that we live in

cues.zh: 是安全可靠的。
cues.en: is safe and sound.

cues.zh: 工程师签署设计方案时，
cues.en: When an engineer seals a design,

cues.zh: 就要为方案的准确性，以及公众的安全负责。
cues.en: he or she takes responsibility for its accuracy and safety to the general public.

cues.zh: 人非圣贤，工程师也不例外。
cues.en: But the err is human and that includes engineers.

cues.zh: 因此，我们努力制定规范和流程，
cues.en: So, we try to develop conventions and processes

cues.zh: 及时发现并纠正错误，避免问题扩大。
cues.en: that can catch and correct from mistakes before they get too far.

cues.zh: 这也包括研究过去的错误，并从中吸取教训。
cues.en: And that includes studying and learning from errors made in the past.

cues.zh: 凯悦酒店连廊坍塌事故是一个重要的案例研究
cues.en: The failure of the Hyatt Regency walkways is an important case study

cues.zh: 几乎每位工程师都会学到这个案例
cues.en: taught to nearly every engineer

cues.zh: 目的是让这样的悲剧不再重演。
cues.en: with the goal that such a tragedy will never occur again.

cues.zh: Practical Engineering 有很多精彩视频，快去订阅吧！
cues.en: Practical Engineering is filled with great videos, so go subscribe!

cues.zh: 我建议先看 Grady 关于静水力学的视频。
cues.en: I would recommend starting with Grady’s video on hydrostatics.

cues.zh: 下次见，
cues.en: Next time,

cues.zh: 将带来一期嘉宾视频，还有一件去过月球的道具。
cues.en: a guest video with a prop that has been to the moon.
